therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: PET radiotracer binding to amyloid beta
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: amyloid beta plaque detection as prognostic biomarker for Alzheimer's disease conversion
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: subjects with amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI)
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Hazard Ratio for conversion to probable Alzheimer's Disease based on visual PET image interpretation (normal vs abnormal) over up to 36 months

results.effect_size: Hazard Ratios ranging from 1.962 to 3.418 across 5 independent readers (abnormal vs normal scan)
results.target_engagement_evidence: Visual PET scan interpretation classified subjects as normal (amyloid negative) or abnormal (amyloid positive); abnormal scans associated with higher conversion rates to probable AD
biomarker_changes: Reader 1: 50/82 abnormal subjects converted to pAD vs 31/142 normal subjects
Reader 2: 60/131 abnormal subjects converted to pAD vs 21/93 normal subjects
Reader 3: 44/79 abnormal subjects converted to pAD vs 37/145 normal subjects
Reader 4: 53/98 abnormal subjects converted to pAD vs 28/126 normal subjects
Reader 5: 52/97 abnormal subjects converted to pAD vs 29/127 normal subjects
Majority reads: 52/97 abnormal subjects converted to pAD vs 29/127 normal subjects
subgroup_findings: Majority reads abnormal: 52/97 converted to pAD; majority reads normal: 29/127 converted to pAD
safety_signals: 1 anaphylactoid reaction (serious adverse event) out of 232 subjects in the flutemetamol arm

context.indication: amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) with risk of conversion to Alzheimer's disease
context.duration: Up to 36 months post flutemetamol administration
context.investigator_commentary: Eight subjects who withdrew prior to the first Clinical Adjudication Committee (CAC) evaluation were not included in the primary analysis (232 - 8 = 224 subjects included).
